changes.headline: Monday settled sharply lower on de-escalation rhetoric with no deal signed, the blockade kept, and Dated Brent at a discount to futures
changes.dek: Monday settles: Brent Jan27 $92.57 (-$5.75, -5.9 percent, lowest since Aug 31), WTI Dec26 $86.85 (-$3.98, -4.4 percent), Brent to WTI spread $5.72 (from $7.49 Friday). Tuesday 0759 GMT: Brent $90.99 (-1.7 percent), WTI $85.20 (-1.8 percent), spread held $5.69 to $5.83. Meeting outcome: no agreement, bridge proposal not accepted, blockade stays, strikes on hold. Morgan Stanley: Dated Brent at a discount to nearby futures.. Monday's session repriced flat price after the presidential meeting with the Qatari prime minister produced no agreement: Brent settled at $92.57, down 5.9 percent and its lowest since Aug 31, WTI settled at $86.85, and Tuesday's Asian session extended the fall to $90.99 and $85.20 on the latest Reuters snapshot. The president's remarks held both halves of the posture: strikes on hold and the war described as effectively over militarily, with the naval blockade explicitly kept and the status quo maintained; the secretary of state called Iran's demands outrageous and the sides not close, and the two-day bridge proposal was not accepted. The factors on the board are that rhetoric, recovering Gulf supply on both October surveys, the Saudi December price cut, the J.P. Morgan surplus estimates of 1.1 Mb/d in September and 1.4 Mb/d in October, and Morgan Stanley's read that Dated Brent at a discount to nearby futures signals a soft physical front. No single factor is established as the driver: the blockade was kept, the proposal was not accepted, and measured flows did not improve, yet the fall continued into Tuesday, which places positioning and physical softness on the board beside diplomacy.
changes.balance_read: Flat price is falling on tone while the Canadian differential's traded strip firms on the basin's own arithmetic, and the Brent to WTI spread at $5.72 keeps the export leg shut. The dated tests of the de-escalation pricing are Abu Dhabi on Nov 10-11 and Thursday's inventory print; the physical gauges currently point in different directions, with Hormuz flows at the visible floor and distillate stocks at their lowest since May 2003.
changes.publishers: Bloomberg via Rigzone, Nov 9, 2026; Reuters, Nov 9-10, 2026; Morgan Stanley note via Reuters, Nov 9, 2026

changes.headline: December WCS marked tighter for a third straight session on zero lots, while January traded 620 lots tighter and Houston's traded volume thinned
changes.dek: TMW Dec26 -$28.91 (+$0.76, 0 lots, third straight zero-lot tightening); Jan27 -$23.35 (+$0.50, 620 lots vs 1 lot Friday); Feb27 -$22.45 (100 lots); Mar27 -$21.45 (100 lots, the one wider tenor); ARV Dec26 -$18.53 (0 lots); ARV Jan27 -$16.10 on 2 lots (vs 725 Friday); ARV Mar27 -$12.80 on 625 lots. ARV to TMW: December +$10.38, January +$7.25. December WCS outright $57.94 on Monday's WTI settle of $86.85.. The Nov 9 ICE file separates the front month from the strip again. December WCS is -$28.91 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 9), marked tighter by $0.76 on zero lots, its third consecutive zero-lot tightening, so the front month still has no traded confirmation at tighter levels. The traded strip behind it firmed for a fourth straight session, and the volume moved: January took 620 lots at -$23.35 against 1 lot on Friday, February 100 lots, and April through June 185 lots each. Houston's traded confirmation went the other way: January ARV printed on only 2 lots against 725 on Friday, with March carrying the Houston volume at 625 lots. December MSW is +$0.45, December SYN +$8.66, December C5 +$9.00 and December UHC +$4.75, each on zero lots (ICE settles, Nov 9).
changes.balance_read: The strip's traded centre of gravity moved from Houston on Friday to Hardisty on Monday, while flat price fell around both. December's mark keeps improving without a trade; the basin arithmetic behind the strip (November apportionment in effect, balance overflow of roughly 200 kb/d a month into tanks) is unchanged, and a traded December settle is still the confirmation the front month lacks.
changes.publishers: ICE Report Center EOD, Nov 9, 2026; ICE Report Center EOD, Nov 6, 2026

changes.headline: Saudi Arabia's East-West bypass pipeline was struck in the Medina region, with operations unaffected, while Qatari LNG loadings recover faster than crude through the strait
changes.dek: East-West pipeline hit Nov 9 in the Medina region: limited fire extinguished, no casualties, operations unaffected (official statement). AIS-visible Hormuz crossings: 5 on Nov 9 (3 tankers), 1 by early Nov 10, 7-day average 7.1 a day, roughly 8 percent of the normal visible rate (a floor gauge, not a flow measure). Qatari LNG loadings: 13 to 15 cargoes per 10-day average in November vs about 11 in October, roughly half the pre-war rate; 11 laden tankers exited in the 10 days to Nov 8.. The bypass infrastructure is now part of the named target set: Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, the kingdom's principal route around the strait, was struck in the Medina region on Nov 9, and the official statement records a limited fire extinguished with no casualties and operations unaffected, so this strike changed no barrel. The flow gauges did not improve with Monday's rhetoric: AIS-visible crossings were 5 on Nov 9 and 1 by early Nov 10, a 7-day average of 7.1 a day, carried as a visibility floor and not a flow measure. Inside the same chokepoint, gas is recovering faster than crude: Qatari LNG loadings run at 13 to 15 cargoes per 10-day average in November against about 11 in October. No new UKMTO or JMIC advisory posted for Nov 9-10; the severe threat assessment stands and the weekend's confirmed tanker events remain confirmed with the mechanism unconfirmed.
changes.balance_read: The corridor's risk price now includes the bypass itself, which raises the cost of the next escalation round without changing today's flows. LNG's faster recovery shows the chokepoint can clear cargoes the crude side is not yet clearing at the same rate, which is a transit-allocation fact, not a crude flow recovery.
changes.publishers: Saudi Energy Ministry via Saudi Press Agency, Nov 9, 2026; Kpler data via Bloomberg and Rigzone, Nov 10, 2026

flags.title: December apportionment: the registered call is Light 14 and Heavy 9, the balance shows about 200 kb/d a month looking for tank space, and nominations close Nov 17
flags.detail: November Mainline apportionment (Light 19 percent at Kerrobert, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert) is in effect from Nov 1. The registered December judgment call is Light 14 percent and Heavy 9 percent. The evidence pack now includes the balance build with November and December supply running about 192 and 216 kb/d above the proven 4,541.6 kb/d egress bound into tanks, a December differential that has marked tighter three straight sessions without trading, a traded January strip firming on volume, and a Brent to WTI spread at $5.72 keeping the export leg shut. December nominations close Tuesday Nov 17; the Enbridge notice follows the close and grades the call. Trigger: The Enbridge December apportionment notice in mid November, or a material change in the November physical backdrop before the nominations close

flags.title: Distillate stocks at their lowest since May 2003: the products leg is the tight part of the US balance into winter
flags.detail: Distillate stocks are 99.3 million barrels, the lowest since May 2003, after a 3.565 million barrel draw in the week ending Oct 30. The validated diesel crack is $86.94, down from $91.19, easing with flat price rather than breaking. The Russian diesel arrangement has produced no confirmed US discharge on the last verified reporting, and Russia's producer diesel export ban runs to Jan 31, 2027. The graded weekly balance scorecard shows the model's crude error channel runs through distillate. The next inventory report is Thursday Nov 12, with the weekly balance forecast and the API print ahead of it. Trigger: The EIA release at 12:00 p.m. ET on Nov 12, a distillate stock build back above 105 million barrels, or a diesel crack break in either direction

flags.title: Price is falling on unsigned rhetoric while the physical gauges point in different directions: the snap-back test is live
flags.detail: Brent settled down 5.9 percent on Monday and fell further on Tuesday after a meeting that produced no agreement, no blockade lift and no accepted proposal, with Hormuz visible crossings at the floor. Against the fall: Dated Brent trades at a discount to futures, J.P. Morgan has the global balance in surplus by 1.1 to 1.4 Mb/d for September and October, and both October OPEC surveys print production recovering. For the other side: the blockade remains enforced, distillate stocks are at a 2003 low, and no flow improvement has been measured. The configuration is the one the causal discipline exists for: factors on the board are listed, and no single driver is established. Trigger: A signed instrument or a measured flow recovery through the strait, a confirmed corridor incident, or the Thursday Nov 12 inventory print

forward_calendar.what: US-hosted Ukraine and Russia talks, Abu Dhabi (Nov 10-11)
forward_calendar.detail: The trilateral round opened today, the first since Geneva on Feb 18, with delegations named on all sides and Europeans on a parallel track. Kyiv wants a ceasefire first; the named gap is Russia's demand for all of Donetsk. Any energy ceasefire language is a products and differentials event first, against a Russian refinery campaign of eight plants struck since Oct 30, the newest hit preliminary.

forward_calendar.what: EIA weekly petroleum report, 12:00 p.m. ET (delayed for Veterans Day)
forward_calendar.detail: The inventory report for the week ending Nov 6 is released a day late for Veterans Day. Distillate at 99.3 million barrels, the lowest since May 2003, is the line that matters; the weekly balance forecast and the API print land ahead of the release.

The deadline for December shipper nominations. The registered December judgment call (Light 14 percent, Heavy 9 percent) grades against the Enbridge notice that follows the close, with the balance showing roughly 200 kb/d a month looking for tank space into the notice.
